title: CameraSwarm Hackers Compromise 14,500+ Dahua Cameras, Backdoor 1,900 Devices
content_md: A threat actor tracked as CameraSwarm compromised more than 14,530 Dahua IP cameras in just 35 days, using mass scanning, weak-password attacks, authentication bypasses, and cloud relay abuse. Investigators found that 1,923 of the affected devices received a persistent backdoor account, potentially allowing attackers to regain access even after an administrator changes the main password. The campaign ran between June 17 and July 22, 2026, and primarily targeted internet-exposed Dahua devices. While scans covered global IP address ranges, confirmed compromises were concentrated in Ukraine and Russia, with the largest number of affected systems located in Ukraine . The campaign also hit networks in Mexico and Vietnam. Researchers uncovered the operation after an attacker-operated server exposed an open HTTP directory. The server contained 2,616 files across 234 folders, including scanning tools, exploitation utilities, stolen-camera records, scripts, and a separate Windows malware payload. CameraSwarm Backdoors Dahua Cameras CameraSwarm used several methods to reach Dahua cameras. Its brute-force engine targeted Dahua’s Easy4IP management service on TCP port 37777, recovering access to 12,324 unique IP addresses. The tool tested credentials at scale and captured camera snapshots after successful logins. It reportedly sent successful credential results to a Telegram channel and saved images locally. The operators also used authentication-bypass techniques associated with CVE-202
